missing_spec_content.spec_text: Some circuits include both series and parallel parts.
missing_spec_content.why: The lesson treats only purely series or purely parallel arrangements. It never mentions circuits that combine both, yet the intro claims 'Knowing both types gives you the tools to work out any circuit you are given.'

missing_spec_content.spec_text: use circuit diagrams to construct and check series and parallel circuits that include a variety of common circuit components
missing_spec_content.why: Every keyPoint has "diagram": null. No circuit symbols or circuit diagrams are shown or explained, and the lesson does not teach how to construct or check circuits from diagrams. The only related content is a short list of meter-placement mistakes. This is despite introTips[2] promising 'you will be able to set up and read circuit diagrams'.

above_gcse.text: An ammeter must have very low resistance, so it doesn't noticeably change the current in the circuit. ... A voltmeter must have very high resistance. Then almost no current goes through it.
above_gcse.why: The specification section does not require the internal resistance of meters. The tutor_note goes further, telling the student 'Just saying where they go is not enough', which puts weight on content the spec does not ask for. This could mislead the student about what is examined.

above_gcse.text: Why ammeters have low resistance and voltmeters high resistance is a frequent exam question.
above_gcse.why: This presents non-specification content as a frequent exam requirement.

factual_errors.text: Both circuit types appear in every paper.
factual_errors.correction: Electricity (section 4.2) is assessed in Physics Paper 1 only, not in every paper.
